# game-qa-mobile

Full guide: SHADDAI Game Forge → guides/11-qa-checklist.md and guides/09-performance.md

## Steps
1. Test on a real mid-range phone, not only an emulator
2. Cap pixel ratio and use the Low quality preset; confirm a steady frame rate for 5 minutes
3. Touch controls: hit areas of at least 44 px, no hover dependence, touch-action: none on the canvas
4. Check orientation changes, safe-area insets and the on-screen keyboard

Phones throttle when hot: test the third minute, not the first.

# threejs-camera-systems

Full guide: SHADDAI Game Forge → guides/03-cameras-and-feel.md and guides/14-interaction-and-controls.md

## Steps
1. Pick the camera for the game type (orbit for strategy, follow for third-person, pointer-lock for first-person, dead-zone follow for side-scrollers)
2. Smooth with exponential damping, not a fixed lerp, so it feels the same at any frame rate
3. Add look-ahead from velocity; ease the vertical axis more slowly
4. Ray-cast from the player to the camera and pull it in front of any wall
5. Shake with trauma squared and smooth noise; give players a reduce-motion option

## Tip
If the camera feels floaty, raise the damping rate; if it feels jittery, add a dead zone.

# Three.js Scene Setup

Create a fully-functional Three.js scene with all foundational components ready to extend.

## What You Get

- Renderer (WebGL with antialiasing, device pixel ratio)
- Orthographic or Perspective camera (adjustable FOV, aspect ratio)
- Default lighting (ambient + directional)
- Animation loop (requestAnimationFrame)
- Responsive resize handling
- Clean teardown

## Usage

```javascript
import { initScene } from './scene-setup.js'

const scene = initScene({
  width: window.innerWidth,
  height: window.innerHeight,
  cameraType: 'perspective',  // 'perspective' or 'orthographic'
  fov: 75,
  ambientLight: 0xffffff,
  directionalLight: 0xffffff,
  backgroundColor: 0x1a1a2e,
  onFrame: (delta) => {
    // Your animation code
  }
})
```

## Example: Spinning Cube

```javascript
const geometry = new THREE.BoxGeometry(1, 1, 1)
const material = new THREE.MeshStandardMaterial({ color: 0x00ff9c })
const cube = new THREE.Mesh(geometry, material)
scene.add(cube)

scene.onFrame = (delta) => {
  cube.rotation.x += delta * 0.5
  cube.rotation.y += delta * 0.5
}
```

## Files

- `scene-setup.js` - Core scene factory
- `camera.js` - Camera utilities
- `lighting.js` - Light presets
- `renderer.js` - Renderer configuration

## References

- [Scene and renderer](../../../../game-forge/guides/01-scene-and-renderer.md)

requires: three.js@r150+, cannon.js OR @react-three/rapier

# Three.js Physics Integration

Connect a physics engine to your Three.js scene for rigidbody dynamics, collisions, and constraints.

## Supported Engines

### Cannon.js
- Classic, stable, pure JavaScript
- Good for general game physics
- Lighter weight

### Rapier WASM
- High-performance Rust-based
- WebAssembly (near-native speed)
- Better for complex simulations

## Setup Example (Cannon.js)

```javascript
import { PhysicsWorld } from './physics-world.js'

const physics = new PhysicsWorld({
  engine: 'cannon',
  gravity: [0, -9.8, 0],
  defaultFriction: 0.3
})

// Create a rigid body
const bodyDesc = physics.createRigidBody({
  shape: 'sphere',
  mass: 1,
  position: [0, 5, 0]
})

const body = physics.addBody(bodyDesc)
const mesh = physics.createVisualFromBody(body)
scene.add(mesh)
```

## Common Shapes

- Box: `{ shape: 'box', size: [1, 1, 1] }`
- Sphere: `{ shape: 'sphere', radius: 1 }`
- Cylinder: `{ shape: 'cylinder', radius: 1, height: 2 }`
- Plane: `{ shape: 'plane' }`

## Frame Update

```javascript
const animate = () => {
  physics.step(1/60)  // Fixed timestep
  
  // Physics automatically syncs to mesh positions
  
  renderer.render(scene, camera)
  requestAnimationFrame(animate)
}
```

## References

- [Cannon.js Docs](https://cannon-es.sparkpost.com/)
- [Physics and collision](../../../../game-forge/guides/06-physics.md)

# Game QA — Performance Profiling

Monitor and optimize your game's performance metrics.

## Metrics Tracked

- **FPS** — Frames per second (target: 60 or 120)
- **Frame Time** — Per-frame execution time (ms)
- **Memory** — Heap usage, geometry memory, texture memory
- **GPU Load** — Draw calls, triangles, pixels
- **Jank** — Frame time variance (stutters)

## Setup

```javascript
import { PerformanceProfiler } from './profiler.js'

const profiler = new PerformanceProfiler({
  captureInterval: 100,  // ms between samples
  historyLength: 60,     // keep last N samples
  warnings: {
    fpsBelowTarget: 55,
    frameTimeCritical: 20,  // ms
    memoryWarning: 150      // MB
  }
})

profiler.start()
```

## Monitoring Frame

```javascript
const animate = () => {
  profiler.frameStart()
  
  // Your game code
  world.update(delta)
  renderer.render(scene, camera)
  
  profiler.frameEnd()
  
  // Print stats every second
  if (profiler.shouldPrintStats()) {
    console.log(profiler.getStats())
    // → {fps: 59.8, avgFrameTime: 16.7, peakMemory: 148}
  }
  
  requestAnimationFrame(animate)
}
```

## Optimization Checklist

- [ ] Cull off-screen objects
- [ ] Use LOD (Level of Detail) for distant meshes
- [ ] Batch similar materials
- [ ] Use instancing for repeated geometry
- [ ] Compress textures (WebP, ASTC)
- [ ] Profile GPU with WebGL Inspector
- [ ] Monitor draw call count (< 500 for 60 FPS)

## References

- [Performance](../../../../game-forge/guides/09-performance.md)
- [Release QA checklist](../../../../game-forge/guides/11-qa-checklist.md)

title: ECS Framework
Game visual review
text:
---
name: game-visual-review
description: See the running game, find what looks wrong or basic, fix the code, and verify the fix visually. Use when: improving how a browser game looks or performs, reviewing someone's game, or when asked to polish, debug a blank/black screen, or "make it look better".
---

# Game visual review

Stop guessing from source code. Run the game, look at it, find the cause, fix it, look again.

Full guide: `game-forge/guides/17-visual-review.md` · Tools: `vision/` · Needs: Playwright (`npm i -D playwright && npx playwright install chromium`).

## The loop
1. **Serve the game** (any static server, e.g. `npx serve .`) and note the URL.
2. **Capture**: `node vision/review.mjs --url <url> --seconds 8 --out reports/before`
   - To exercise the game, pass `--actions actions.json` (keys, clicks, typing at given seconds).
   - Optional: expose `window.__gameProbe = () => ({ drawCalls: renderer.info.render.calls, triangles: renderer.info.render.triangles })` for render stats.
3. **Look first, read second.** Open `reports/before/contact.png`, then each `shot-NN.png`. Write down what you see in plain words *before* reading the findings, so the automatic checks do not bias you.
4. **Read `REPORT.md`.** Each finding gives evidence, which guide to read, and a hint.
5. **Find the cause in code** (grep for the renderer, camera, lights, materials, loop, input handlers). Fix **one root cause at a time**, smallest change that works.
6. **Re-capture** to `reports/after` and run `node vision/compare.mjs reports/before reports/after`.
   Keep the change only if the verdict is IMPROVED or the visual look is better with no new findings.
7. **Repeat** until: no critical findings · frame rate at target · the contact sheet looks intentional · two clean passes in a row. Log each round in `docs/review-log.md` (what you saw, what you changed, result).

## What to look for in the screenshots
| You see | Likely code cause | Read |
|---|---|---|
| Blank/black/one flat colour | camera facing away or inside geometry; no lights; canvas size 0; loop not running | guides 01, 03 |
| Everything one grey, no depth | placeholder materials, no key light, no shadows, ambient only | 04, 15 |
| Looks identical every frame | no idle motion, or inputs not reaching the game | 02, 14 |
| Objects cut off / popping | near/far planes, z-fighting, camera collision | 01, 03 |
| Jagged or shimmering edges | antialias off, pixel ratio 1, wrong texture filtering | 01, 13 |
| Text unreadable or overlapping | HUD sized in pixels at one resolution, no contrast | 14 |
| Tiny or huge objects | inconsistent scale; camera distance/FOV | 03 |
| Empty screen with one object | no environment, no sense of place | 04, 16 |
| Stutter or low fps | too many draw calls, allocations per frame, shadow cost | 09 |
| Actions have no visible feedback | missing hit flashes, shake, particles, squash/stretch | 03 |

## Rules
- The automatic checks catch breakage and basics. They **cannot judge taste**, so always look.
- Change one thing per round, or you will not know what helped.
- If a fix makes one finding disappear and another appear, revert and rethink.
- Keep screenshots of the first and last run; they prove the improvement.

title: SHADDAI Atelier 3D
text:
# SHADDAI Atelier 3D

Turn one image into a verified 3D model (`.glb`) — with a provenance record that says what made it, under which licence, and proves the file hasn't been swapped.

SHADDAI-original code. Pure Python standard library; no GPU or heavy packages required to run the pipeline itself.

## Why
Image-to-3D services and local models all have different licences, and outputs get renamed and passed around. Atelier 3D keeps a small `.provenance.json` next to every model so you always know where it came from and whether you may use it commercially.

## Quick start
```bash
cd shaddai-3d-atelier
python -m pytest -q                                  # 24 tests, no network
python -m atelier3d backends --config backends.example.json
python -m atelier3d image hero.png --config backends.json --backend local-gpu --out out --faces 5000 --commercial
python -m atelier3d text "a stone lantern" --config backends.json --backend text-gen --out out
python -m atelier3d image hero.png --config backends.json --backend cloud-gen --cloud   # stop at the point-cloud stage
python -m atelier3d cloud out/hero-ab12cd34ef.ply --config backends.json --backend mesher   # point cloud -> mesh, lineage recorded
python -m atelier3d manifest run.json --config backends.json      # repeat a recorded run
python -m atelier3d compare out/a.glb out/b.glb
python -m atelier3d verify out/hero-1a2b3c4d5e.glb   # OK, or exactly what changed
```

## What it does
1. Takes an **image**, a **text prompt**, or a **point cloud** (`.ply`) as input and validates it (type, size, prompt length, finite coordinates).
2. Runs a **backend** — any local program, or a hosted service that works as submit → poll → download. Backends live in a JSON config, so adding one needs no code.
3. Rejects broken output (truncated, empty, zero triangles) with a clear reason.
4. Optionally **decimates** to a face budget (`--faces N`; needs `trimesh` + `fast_simplification`).
5. Writes `<model>.glb.provenance.json`: input hash, output hash, backend + version, licence, warnings for your declared use, timings. The record is itself hashed, so hand edits are detected.

## Backends
```json
{"backends": {
  "local-gpu": {"kind": "command", "command": ["python", "run.py", "{image}", "{out}"],
                 "license": "hunyuan-community", "version": "2.1", "timeout": 1800},
  "hosted":    {"kind": "job", "submit_url": "https://api.example/v1/jobs",
                 "status_url": "https://api.example/v1/jobs/{id}", "token_env": "MY_API_KEY",
                 "license": "service-terms"}}}
```
Commands run without a shell, so image paths can't inject anything. API keys come from environment variables, never the config.

## Licences
`atelier3d/licenses.py` carries short reminders for common weights (Hunyuan community, Stability community, hosted-service terms, permissive, your own). They are **reminders, not legal advice** — terms change, so read the source before shipping.

## Layout
| File | Role |
|---|---|
| `atelier3d/pipeline.py` | `run()` — the whole flow |
| `atelier3d/backends.py` | command and job backends, JSON config loader |
| `atelier3d/glbcheck.py` | stdlib GLB inspector (triangle/mesh/material counts) |
| `atelier3d/ply.py` | stdlib point-cloud reader/validator/writer (binary + ASCII PLY) |
| `atelier3d/compare.py` | side-by-side model comparison (size, geometry, backend, licence) |
| `atelier3d/provenance.py` | build / write / verify records |
| `atelier3d/licenses.py` | licence registry and warnings |
| `atelier3d/finish.py` | optional decimation |
| `atelier3d/cli.py` | `image`, `text`, `cloud`, `manifest`, `compare`, `verify`, `backends` |

## Use from TURTLE
Point a backend at your preferred generator, run the CLI from the design studio, then hand the verified `.glb` to the game's loader (see `game-forge/guides/04-assets-and-materials.md`).

title: 02 · The game loop
text:
# 02 · The game loop

Rendering speed varies by device; game rules must not. Separate them.

## The rule
**Simulate in fixed slices. Render whenever the browser says so, blending between the last two simulated states.**

`runtime/fixed-step.mjs` does this:
```js
import { FixedStep, blend } from './runtime/fixed-step.mjs';

const loop = new FixedStep({
  hz: 60,
  update: (dt) => world.step(dt),          // always 1/60 s
  render: (alpha) => {                     // 0..1 progress to the next slice
    for (const m of movers) m.mesh.position.x = blend(m.prevX, m.x, alpha);
    renderer.render(scene, camera);
  },
});
renderer.setAnimationLoop((ms) => loop.tick(ms / 1000));
```

## Why it matters
- **Same behaviour everywhere.** A 144 Hz laptop and a 30 Hz phone get identical physics and identical replays.
- **Stable physics.** Integrators and collision resolve badly with wildly varying `dt`.
- **Deterministic tests.** Feed 600 ticks into the world and assert the result — no browser needed.

## Stall protection
Tabs pause. Debuggers pause. Without a cap the loop returns after a minute and tries to simulate 3,600 steps at once. `maxCatchUp` (default 0.25 s) drops the backlog instead. Pair it with the Page Visibility API: pause audio and timers on `visibilitychange`.

## Store previous state
For interpolation, each mover needs `prev` and `curr`. Copy `curr → prev` at the **start** of each update, then integrate. Teleports (respawns) should set both so the mesh doesn't streak across the map.

## Time you can trust
- Use the simulation clock (`world.time`) for gameplay timers: cooldowns, spawn waves, status effects.
- Use the wall clock only for presentation: UI fades, camera shake decay, particle lifetime.
- Never use `Date.now()` for gameplay; it breaks pause and replay.

## Slow-motion and pause
Scale `dt` before it reaches `world.step` (`dt * timeScale`). Pausing is `timeScale = 0`; the render side keeps drawing, so menus and camera still animate.

title: 06 · Physics and collision
text:
# 06 · Physics and collision

Pick the lightest tool that gives the behaviour you need.

| Your game needs | Use | Cost |
|---|---|---|
| Platformer, top-down, blocky worlds | **Box sweeps** (`runtime/collide.mjs`) | Tiny |
| Picking, line of sight, ground checks | **Ray casts** | Tiny |
| Stacking crates, rolling balls, ragdolls | A full rigid-body engine (WASM) | Significant |
| Vehicles, joints, constraints | A full rigid-body engine | Significant |

Most games never need the last two. Reach for a heavy engine only when stacking, tumbling or joints are core to the fun.

## Character controllers (platformers)
Use a **kinematic** controller: you decide velocity, the collision code only stops you. Don't make the player a free-tumbling rigid body.
```js
body.vy -= GRAVITY * dt;                        // 30–40 u/s² feels punchy; real gravity feels floaty
body.vy = Math.max(body.vy, -TERMINAL);
const { box, hit } = moveAndSlide(body, { x: body.vx * dt, y: body.vy * dt }, solids);
Object.assign(body, box);
if (hit.y) { if (body.vy < 0) grounded = true; body.vy = 0; }
if (hit.x) body.vx = 0;
```
Add **variable jump height** (cut `vy` when the button is released early), **coyote time** and a **jump buffer** (`runtime/actions.mjs`). These three change feel more than any physics tuning.

## Broad phase when you have many bodies
Brute-force overlap tests are fine below ~100 bodies. Beyond that, bucket bodies into a uniform grid keyed by cell (`Math.floor(x / cell)`), and only test neighbours in the same or adjacent cells.

## Tunnelling
A fast body can skip entirely over a thin wall between two frames. `moveAndSlide` sub-steps automatically. For projectiles, ray cast along the path travelled this tick instead of testing the end position.

## Determinism
Fixed timestep (guide 02) + no `Math.random` in physics + a fixed iteration order = identical results on every machine. That unlocks replays, rollback netcode, and reliable automated tests.

## Debug it visually
Draw every collider as a wireframe box in a toggleable layer. Most "physics bugs" are a collider that isn't where you think it is.

title: 11 · Release QA checklist
text:
# 11 · Release QA checklist

Run top to bottom before any build goes to players. Record pass/fail and the build id.

## Plays right
- [ ] New player reaches the first goal without help in under 2 minutes
- [ ] Every verb has visual, audio and (where relevant) haptic feedback
- [ ] Death/failure restarts in under 3 seconds
- [ ] No soft-locks: try to get stuck on purpose in each level
- [ ] Difficulty curve: the first 5 minutes are easy, the rest escalates

## Runs right
- [ ] Holds target frame rate on the slowest supported device (low preset)
- [ ] No frame-time spikes over 50 ms during normal play
- [ ] Memory stays flat over a 30-minute session (no leak growth)
- [ ] Loading time under 5 s on a mid-range connection; progress is shown
- [ ] Tab hidden → returns without a burst of catch-up or stuck audio

## Works everywhere
- [ ] Latest Chrome, Safari, Firefox, and one mobile browser
- [ ] Window resize, orientation change, DPR change handled
- [ ] Keyboard, mouse, touch and (if promised) gamepad all work; no stuck keys after focus loss
- [ ] Remappable or at least discoverable controls

## Accessible
- [ ] Text readable at phone size; contrast meets WCAG AA
- [ ] Information never carried by colour alone
- [ ] Sound is not required to play; subtitles for spoken lines
- [ ] Reduce-motion option disables shake, flashes and parallax
- [ ] No flashing faster than 3 times per second

## Safe
- [ ] Client is never trusted for scores, currency or unlocks — the server validates
- [ ] Inputs sanitised; saves can't be edited to crash or grant rewards
- [ ] No secrets or API keys in shipped code
- [ ] Rate limits on anything that costs money or hits an external service
- [ ] Privacy: only collect what's needed; say what and why

## Release hygiene
- [ ] Version number visible in the menu
- [ ] Error reporting wired; test error shows up
- [ ] Rollback plan: the previous build is one step away
- [ ] Known issues list written, even if short

## Automated checks worth having
- Deterministic simulation test: run N ticks from a seed, assert a hash of final state.
- Collision unit tests (floors, walls, corners, fast movers).
- A "monkey" run: random inputs for 5 minutes must not crash.

title: 03 · Cameras and game feel
text:
# 03 · Cameras and game feel

A camera is a character. Players judge a game's quality within seconds largely by how it moves.

## Follow camera with smoothing that doesn't lag
Plain `lerp(camera, target, 0.1)` is frame-rate dependent: it feels different at 30 and 144 fps. Use an exponential decay instead:

```js
// k = how quickly we close the gap (per second). 6–12 feels snappy, 2–4 feels floaty.
const damp = (current, target, k, dt) => target + (current - target) * Math.exp(-k * dt);

camera.position.x = damp(camera.position.x, player.x + offset.x, 8, dt);
camera.position.y = damp(camera.position.y, player.y + offset.y, 5, dt);   // slower on Y = less nausea
camera.position.z = damp(camera.position.z, player.z + offset.z, 8, dt);
camera.lookAt(player.x, player.y + 1, player.z);
```

## Look-ahead
Shift the focus point toward where the player is *going*: `focus = player + velocity * 0.25`. The player sees more of what's coming; the camera feels intelligent.

## Dead zone
In 2D and side-scrollers, let the player move inside a small box before the camera follows. Constant tracking makes tiny movements feel jittery.

## Collision-aware third-person
Cast a ray from the player's head to the desired camera spot (`collide.mjs → raycast`). If it hits geometry, put the camera just in front of the hit. Ease back out slowly once the view clears.

## Shake that reads as impact
```js
// trauma ∈ [0,1], raised by hits and decayed over time; shake grows with trauma².
const s = trauma * trauma;
camera.rotation.z = s * 0.05 * noise(t * 30);
camera.position.x += s * 0.3 * noise(t * 27 + 10);
trauma = Math.max(0, trauma - dt * 1.4);
```
Use smooth noise, not `Math.random()`, or the shake looks like static. Shake rotation more than position.

## Juice checklist (do these before adding content)
- **Hit stop:** freeze the simulation 50–90 ms on a heavy hit.
- **Squash and stretch:** scale the sprite or mesh 10–20% on jump and landing, restoring over ~120 ms.
- **Input forgiveness:** buffer presses and allow coyote time (`runtime/actions.mjs`).
- **Audio on every verb:** jump, land, hit, pickup. Silence reads as broken.
- **Particles on contact:** a few short-lived puffs sell weight.
- **FOV kick:** widen the field of view 3–6° when sprinting; ease it back.

title: 12 · Animation
08 · 2D sprites and animation
text:
# 08 · 2D sprites and animation

## Sheet layout
Put a character's frames in a **grid**: one row per action (idle, walk, jump, attack), one column per frame. Equal cell size, transparent background, feet on the same baseline in every frame so the character doesn't bob when clips switch.

```js
import { gridSheet, clip } from './runtime/clips.mjs';
const sheet = gridSheet({ cols: 8, rows: 4, frameW: 64, frameH: 64 });
const clips = {
  idle:   clip(sheet, { row: 0, from: 0, to: 3, fps: 6,  mode: 'loop' }),
  run:    clip(sheet, { row: 1, from: 0, to: 7, fps: 14, mode: 'loop' }),
  attack: clip(sheet, { row: 2, from: 0, to: 5, fps: 18, mode: 'once' }),
};
const frame = clips[state].at(timeInState);        // → { x, y, w, h, u, v, uw, vh }
```
Clips are pure functions of time, so pausing, slow-motion and replay need no extra state.

## Drawing
- **Canvas 2D:** `ctx.drawImage(img, f.x, f.y, f.w, f.h, dx, dy, f.w, f.h)`; set `ctx.imageSmoothingEnabled = false` for crisp pixel art.
- **three.js:** a plane with a `MeshBasicMaterial`, `transparent: true`; set the texture's `repeat` to `(f.uw, f.vh)` and `offset` to `(f.u, f.v)`. Use `NearestFilter` for pixel art.

## State machine, not flags
Drive the clip from a state (`idle → run → jump → fall → land`). On state change reset `timeInState` to 0. Transitions are explicit; no tangle of booleans.

## Timing feel
- 8–14 fps reads as hand-drawn and charming; 24+ looks smooth but costs more art.
- Hold the **contact frame** of attacks a beat longer; it sells impact more than extra frames do.
- Anticipation (a small wind-up) + follow-through (a settle) matter more than frame count.

## Pixel art at any screen size
Render the game at a small fixed resolution (e.g. 320×180) and scale the canvas by an **integer** factor. Non-integer scaling shimmers.

## Layering
Draw by **y-order** in top-down games (lower on screen = in front). Separate parallax layers move at fractions of camera speed (far = 0.2, mid = 0.5, near = 1.0).

## Production tips
- Keep a source layered file per character; export sheets by script so a tweak is one command.
- Name clips consistently across characters (`idle`, `run`, `attack`) so the same controller code drives any of them.
- Generated art needs the same checks as hand-drawn: consistent baseline, consistent palette, no stray edge pixels.

title: 16 · Panoramas and skyboxes
text:
# 16 · Panoramas and skyboxes

A 360° image can be a **skybox** (backdrop for a game), a **reflection source** (environment map), or the whole experience (a panorama viewer). Two formats cover almost everything:

| Format | Shape | Best for |
|---|---|---|
| **Equirectangular** | one 2:1 image (e.g. 2048×1024) | what cameras, AI generators and HDRI sites produce; easy to author and store |
| **Cube map** | six square faces | what GPUs sample fastest; sharper at the same memory; best for skyboxes |

`runtime/panorama.mjs` handles the maths both ways:
```js
import { detectLayout, equirectToCubeFace, FACES } from './runtime/panorama.mjs';
detectLayout(2048, 1024);                          // 'equirect'
const faces = Object.fromEntries(FACES.map((f) => [f, equirectToCubeFace(img, f, 1024)]));
```

## Using one in three.js
```js
const tex = new THREE.TextureLoader().load('sky.jpg');
tex.mapping = THREE.EquirectangularReflectionMapping;
tex.colorSpace = THREE.SRGBColorSpace;
scene.background = tex;          // visible backdrop
scene.environment = tex;         // lights Standard materials
```
For a viewer, put the camera at the centre of an inside-out sphere (`geometry.scale(-1, 1, 1)`) textured with the image, then rotate the camera with drag (yaw/pitch, clamp pitch to ±85°) and zoom by changing field of view (30–100°). `panorama-viewer.html` is a minimal example.

## Making good panoramas
- **Ratio matters:** exactly 2:1 for equirectangular. A wrong ratio stretches everything.
- **Seam:** the left and right edges must match. Generators often leave a visible seam; blend a strip across it, or mirror-wrap-edit before use.
- **Poles:** the top and bottom rows are stretched to a point, so detail there looks smeared. Keep important content near the horizon.
- **Resolution:** a 360° view shows only ~90° at a time, so a 4096×2048 map gives about 1000 px across the screen. 2048×1024 is a floor for quality.
- **HDR:** for lighting, use a high-dynamic-range format (`.hdr`/`.exr`); an 8-bit JPEG can't light a scene realistically.

## Pitfalls
- Flipped image: check handedness — viewing from inside mirrors the texture unless you flip the sphere or the u axis.
- Blurry skybox: texture too small, or mipmaps filtering a skybox that should use linear filtering with no mipmaps.
- Banding in gradients: add 1–2 LSB of noise before saving to 8-bit.

title: 04 · Assets, lighting and materials
text:
# 04 · Assets, lighting and materials

## Formats
| Need | Use | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| 3D models | **glTF / GLB** | The web standard; carries meshes, materials, skeletons, animations |
| Small downloads | Draco or meshopt compression | Compress geometry once at build time |
| GPU-friendly textures | **KTX2 (Basis)** | Stays compressed in video memory; JPG/PNG expand to full size |
| Sprites | PNG sheets or WebP | Keep power-of-two atlas dimensions for mipmaps |
| Audio | OGG/AAC for music, short WAV/OGG for effects | Decode effects once, keep buffers |

## Loading without a stall
- Show a loading screen driven by a real progress counter (`LoadingManager`).
- Load in tiers: **boot** (menu, player), **level** (current area), **stream** (next area, decorative props).
- Cache by URL. Two requests for the same file should share one promise.
- Decode off the main thread where possible (`ImageBitmapLoader`, worker-based KTX2/Draco decoders).

```js
const cache = new Map();
export const load = (url, loader) =>
  cache.get(url) ?? cache.set(url, loader.loadAsync(url)).get(url);
```

## Materials: pick the cheapest that looks right
1. **MeshBasicMaterial** — unlit. Free. Great for UI planes, skyboxes, stylised flat looks.
2. **MeshLambertMaterial** — cheap diffuse lighting.
3. **MeshStandardMaterial** — physically based; use for hero assets.
4. **ShaderMaterial** — custom look (guide 05) when the built-ins can't do it.

Share material instances between meshes. Fifty crates with fifty identical materials cost fifty draw states; one shared material is one.

## Lighting for games
- **One key light** (directional) + **a hemisphere or ambient fill**. More lights = more shader cost per pixel.
- Bake what never moves: lightmaps and baked AO beat dynamic lights for static scenery.
- Environment maps (a small HDR) make Standard materials look right with almost no extra lights.
- Cheap fake shadows (a dark blob decal under characters) are fine for crowds.

## Colour discipline
Colour textures (albedo/emissive) are sRGB; data textures (normal, roughness, metalness, AO) are linear. Mixing them up is the number-one reason "the colours look wrong".

## Instancing
Many copies of one mesh? `InstancedMesh` draws thousands in a single call. Update per-instance transforms with `setMatrixAt` and flag `instanceMatrix.needsUpdate = true` once per frame, not per instance.

title: 10 · Running a game project
text:
# 10 · Running a game project

A small game is a sequence of decisions made in a good order. This is SHADDAI's order.

## Roles (people or agents)
| Role | Owns | SHADDAI agent |
|---|---|---|
| Director | the one-sentence pitch, scope, final call | SHADDAI |
| Engineer | loop, systems, tools, performance | NEXUS |
| Designer | rules, balance, level flow, onboarding | ORACLE |
| Artist | look, characters, UI, animation | TURTLE |
| Writer | text, tutorials, store copy | QUILL |
| QA / security | breakage, exploits, cheating, privacy | PIKADON |
| Economy | pricing, rewards, sinks and sources | ZEROX |

One person can wear several hats. The point is that every decision has an owner.

## Gates — don't skip a gate to save a day
1. **Pitch.** One sentence: *who* does *what* and why it's fun. If it needs two sentences it is two games.
2. **Core loop prototype.** Grey boxes, one mechanic, 30 seconds of play. If this isn't fun, stop or change it; art can't rescue it.
3. **Vertical slice.** One short level at final quality — art, sound, UI, feel. It sets the bar for everything else.
4. **Content pass.** Build the remaining levels, enemies and items using the systems the slice proved.
5. **Polish and balance.** Feel, difficulty curve, onboarding, performance ladder.
6. **Release candidate.** Feature freeze. Only fixes. Run the QA checklist (guide 11).
7. **Ship and listen.** Instrument it, read feedback, patch in small steps.

## Design document: one page
- Pitch (one sentence) · target player · platform and input
- Core loop (verbs → feedback → goal)
- Failure and restart (how quickly, how kindly)
- Progression (what changes over time)
- Scope list: **must**, **should**, **could**. Cut from the bottom first.
- Risks (the three things most likely to sink it) and how you'll test each early

## Scope control
- Estimate in days, then double it.
- Every new idea goes on the "could" list, not into the build.
- A feature that needs a new system, new art and new UI at once is three features.

## Playtesting
Watch someone play without helping. Note where they hesitate, where they laugh, where they quit. Five players find most problems. Fix the problem you saw, not the solution they suggested.

## Working with agents
Give each agent a role, a gate, and a definition of done. Hand work over as files (design doc, shot list, asset list), not chat. Have a different agent review than the one that built.

title: 15 · Post-processing and finishing
text:
# 15 · Post-processing and finishing

Post-processing renders the scene to an off-screen image, then runs full-screen passes over it. It's the cheapest way to give a game a *look* — and the easiest way to wreck performance, because every pass touches every pixel.

## Pipeline shape
```
scene → render target → [bloom] → [colour grade] → [vignette] → [anti-alias / output] → screen
```
Use an effect-composer style chain: one render pass, then your effects, then an output pass that handles tone mapping and colour space once.

## Effects worth having
| Effect | What it sells | Cost | Tip |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Bloom** | glow on lights, magic, UI emissives | medium | Raise the *threshold* so only bright things bloom; low strength, wide radius |
| **Colour grading** | mood and cohesion | cheap | A tiny 3D LUT or three sliders (contrast, saturation, tint) |
| **Vignette** | focus, cinematic frame | cheap | Keep it subtle (≤0.25) |
| **Outline** | readable silhouettes, stylised look | medium | Depth/normal edge detection; skip on mobile |
| **Depth of field** | scale and focus | expensive | Prefer fake blur on backgrounds |
| **Chromatic aberration / film grain** | impact flashes, texture | cheap | Pulse on hits, not constant |
| **FXAA/SMAA** | smooth edges when MSAA is off | cheap | Use when post-processing disables native antialiasing |

## Rules
1. **Budget passes.** Each full-screen pass costs roughly one more screen's worth of pixel work. On low quality, run none or one.
2. **Render at lower resolution** for expensive passes (bloom works fine at half resolution).
3. **Do tone mapping once**, at the end, not in each pass.
4. **Make effects driven by game state:** brief bloom/aberration spikes on explosions, desaturation at low health, tint by biome. Static filters get ignored; reactive ones get noticed.
5. **Always provide a toggle** (accessibility and performance): reduce-motion disables flashes, shake and aberration.

## Cheaper alternatives
- Fake glow: an additive, softly-textured quad behind bright objects.
- Fake fog: scene `Fog` or a gradient to the sky colour — one line, no pass.
- Baked colour: bake grading into textures and lighting for static scenes.

## Check list before shipping a look
- Looks right on both dark and bright scenes.
- Text and UI stay crisp (draw UI after post-processing or in HTML).
- Frame time with effects on stays inside the quality ladder (guide 09).

title: 13 · Geometry and textures
text:
# 13 · Geometry and textures

## Geometry
A mesh is a list of vertices plus triangles (indices). Built-ins (`BoxGeometry`, `SphereGeometry`, `PlaneGeometry`, `CylinderGeometry`) cover prototypes. Build your own with `BufferGeometry`:

```js
const geo = new THREE.BufferGeometry();
geo.setAttribute('position', new THREE.Float32BufferAttribute([0,0,0,  1,0,0,  0,1,0], 3));
geo.setAttribute('uv',       new THREE.Float32BufferAttribute([0,0,  1,0,  0,1], 2));
geo.setIndex([0, 1, 2]);
geo.computeVertexNormals();
```

### Rules of thumb
- Segment counts: spheres rarely need more than 32×16; flat planes need 1×1 unless you displace them.
- **Merge** static scenery into few meshes; **instance** repeated props.
- Update vertex data sparingly: set `attribute.needsUpdate = true` once per frame at most, and prefer doing motion in a vertex shader.
- Recentre geometry (`geo.center()`) so rotation pivots where you expect.
- Bounding volumes drive culling; after changing vertices call `geo.computeBoundingSphere()`.

## Procedural worlds
Heightmap terrain: a subdivided plane whose vertex `y` comes from layered noise (`sum of noise(x·f)·a` for a few octaves). Chunk it (e.g. 64×64 tiles) so you can build, hide and dispose by region.

## Textures
| Kind | Colour space | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Albedo / emissive | sRGB | what you see |
| Normal, roughness, metalness, AO | Linear | raw data — never colour-managed |

- **Mipmaps** on (default) for anything that shrinks with distance; off for UI and pixel art.
- **Anisotropy** (`texture.anisotropy = 4`) sharpens textures seen at grazing angles, like floors.
- Pixel art: `magFilter = minFilter = NearestFilter`, no mipmaps.
- Tiling: `wrapS = wrapT = RepeatWrapping`, then set `repeat`.
- Pack channels: store roughness, metalness and AO in one texture's R/G/B to cut texture reads.

## Atlases
One big texture with many sub-images means one material and one draw call. Offset UVs per sprite or tile; leave 1–2 px padding between cells to prevent bleeding when filtered.

## Generated textures
Draw to a small `<canvas>` and wrap it in `CanvasTexture` for dynamic labels, minimaps or procedural patterns; call `texture.needsUpdate = true` after each redraw, and keep them small.

## Memory
Texture memory is width × height × 4 bytes × ~1.33 (mips). A 2048² texture is ~22 MB on the GPU, no matter how small its file. Budget by that number, and compress (KTX2) for anything large.

title: 14 · Interaction and controls
07 · Entities, components and systems
09 · Performance
text:
# 09 · Performance

Target **60 fps on the weakest device you care about**. Measure first, change one thing, measure again.

## Know the budget
Per frame at 60 fps you have **16.6 ms**, shared between your code, the browser, and the GPU. Aim to use ~10 ms so spikes don't drop frames.

## Find the bottleneck before fixing anything
| Symptom | Likely cause | First test |
|---|---|---|
| FPS rises a lot when you shrink the window | **Fill-rate / pixel-bound** (heavy shaders, big transparents, high DPR) | Lower `setPixelRatio` |
| FPS unchanged by window size, CPU thread pegged | **CPU-bound** (too many draw calls, heavy JS) | Check `renderer.info.render.calls` |
| Periodic hitches every few seconds | **Garbage collection** | Look for per-frame allocations |
| Hitch when something first appears | **Shader compile / texture upload** | Pre-warm: render it once off-screen at load |

## The big wins, in order
1. **Cut draw calls.** Aim for under ~300. Merge static geometry, share materials, use `InstancedMesh` for repeats.
2. **Cap resolution.** `min(devicePixelRatio, 2)`, and offer a quality slider that drops to 1.
3. **Fewer, cheaper lights and shadows.** One shadow-casting light; bake the rest.
4. **Cull.** Frustum culling is automatic; add distance culling and room/zone visibility for large worlds.
5. **LOD.** Swap to cheaper meshes or billboards at distance.
6. **Texture memory.** Use compressed (KTX2) textures; downscale anything that never appears large.

## Don't allocate in the hot path
Creating `new Vector3()` or `{}` every frame feeds the garbage collector and causes hitches.
```js
const tmp = new THREE.Vector3();          // allocate once, reuse
function update() { tmp.copy(a).sub(b).normalize(); }
```
Pool short-lived things (bullets, particles, damage numbers): keep an array of inactive objects, grab one, reset it, return it when done.

## Update less often what you can
Run AI at 10 Hz, not 60. Update far-away entities every few frames. Sleep entities with nothing to do.

## Particles
Use one `Points` or `InstancedMesh` for thousands of particles and animate them in the vertex shader from a start time and seed. Simulating each in JS doesn't scale.

## Measure on a real low-end device
A mid-range phone shows problems your desktop hides. Test early, and test on the slowest target regularly, not once at the end.

## Build a quality ladder
Low / Medium / High presets that change pixel ratio, shadow size, particle counts and draw distance. Auto-select by measuring the first few seconds of frame time, and let the player override.

title: 17 · Seeing your game: visual review
text:
# 17 · Seeing your game: visual review

Reading code tells you what a game *should* do. Looking at it tells you what it *does*. A visual review loop lets an agent (or you) run the game, look at real frames, and fix what is wrong without coding blind over and over.

## The tools (`vision/`)
| File | Does |
|---|---|
| `review.mjs` | Runs the game in headless Chromium, takes screenshots, records console output, failed requests, frame rate and optional draw calls; writes `contact.png`, `shot-NN.png`, `report.json`, `REPORT.md` |
| `analyze.mjs` | Turns the numbers into findings: what is wrong, the evidence, where to look |
| `compare.mjs` | Before/after: findings fixed or introduced, performance change, how much of each screenshot changed |
| `metrics.mjs`, `png.mjs` | Dependency-free image maths and PNG reading/writing |

Run the tests with `node vision/vision.test.mjs`.

## Running it
```bash
npx serve .                                            # or any static server
node vision/review.mjs --url http://localhost:3000 --seconds 8 --out reports/before
```
Make the game play itself with an actions file:
```json
[
  { "at": 1.0, "key": "ArrowRight", "hold": 0.6 },
  { "at": 2.5, "key": "Space" },
  { "at": 4.0, "click": [640, 360] }
]
```
Optional render stats — add one line to your game:
```js
window.__gameProbe = () => ({ drawCalls: renderer.info.render.calls, triangles: renderer.info.render.triangles });
```

## What the automatic checks catch
Blank or flat frames · a picture that never changes (and whether inputs were sent) · over/under-exposure · very few colours · console errors and warnings · missing assets (404s) · low fps and frame spikes · too many draw calls or triangles.

## What only looking can catch
Composition, scale and proportion, whether the hero is readable, the mood of the lighting, UI overlap, visual hierarchy, and whether it feels like a place rather than a test scene. After reading the report, always open `contact.png` and judge it as a player would.

## Habits that make it work
1. **Look before you read.** Describe the screenshots in words first, then read the findings.
2. **One root cause per round.** Fix, re-capture, compare.
3. **Keep evidence.** Save the first and last runs and a short log of what changed.
4. **Test the experience, not only the first frame.** Use actions to reach the part of the game you changed.
5. **Check small screens too.** Run once with `--width 390 --height 844` for a phone-size view.

## Limits
Headless Chromium uses software rendering when no GPU is available, so measured frame rates are lower than on a real device; use them for relative changes (before vs after) rather than absolute targets.

"""Licence notes for the model weights and services a backend may use.

This is a reminder system, not legal advice: terms change, so each entry links to the
source of truth and the pipeline repeats the warning in every provenance record.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class LicenseTerms:
    id: str
    name: str
    commercial: str      # "yes" | "conditional" | "no" | "service" | "unknown"
    notes: str
    url: str = ""


REGISTRY: dict[str, LicenseTerms] = {t.id: t for t in (
    LicenseTerms(
        "hunyuan-community", "Tencent Hunyuan Community License", "conditional",
        "Typically excludes some territories (EU, UK, South Korea), requires a separate licence "
        "at very large user scale, and limits using outputs to train other AI models. Read the "
        "current text before commercial use.",
        "https://github.com/Tencent-Hunyuan"),
    LicenseTerms(
        "stability-community", "Stability AI Community License", "conditional",
        "Free for non-commercial use and for organisations under an annual-revenue threshold; "
        "above it an enterprise licence is needed. Check the current threshold.",
        "https://stability.ai/license"),
    LicenseTerms(
        "service-terms", "Hosted service terms of use", "service",
        "Rights in outputs are set by the provider's terms and your plan. Keep a copy of the "
        "terms that applied on the generation date.", ""),
    LicenseTerms(
        "permissive", "Permissive open licence (MIT/Apache-2.0/BSD)", "yes",
        "Keep the copyright and licence notices that come with the model.", ""),
    LicenseTerms(
        "own", "Your own model or weights", "yes", "You set the terms.", ""),
)}

UNKNOWN = LicenseTerms("unknown", "Unrecorded licence", "unknown",
                       "No licence was recorded for this backend. Find out before shipping.")


def terms_for(license_id: str) -> LicenseTerms:
    return REGISTRY.get(license_id, UNKNOWN)


def warnings(license_id: str, commercial_use: bool) -> list[str]:
    """Human-readable cautions for using this backend's output the way you said you would."""
    t = terms_for(license_id)
    if t.id == "unknown":
        return [t.notes]
    if commercial_use and t.commercial in ("conditional", "service"):
        return [f"{t.name}: {t.notes}"]
    if commercial_use and t.commercial == "no":
        return [f"{t.name} does not allow commercial use."]
    return []

"""Command line:  python -m atelier3d <command>

  image  IMAGE  --config C --backend B [--out DIR] [--faces N] [--commercial] [--cloud] [--param K=V]
  text   "a stone lantern" --config C --backend B [...same options]
  cloud  CLOUD.ply --config C --backend B [--out DIR] [--faces N]     point cloud -> mesh
  manifest FILE.json --config C                                        repeat a recorded run
  compare A.glb B.glb
  verify MODEL                                                         check a model/cloud against its record
  backends --config C
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import json
import sys
from pathlib import Path

from . import provenance
from .backends import load_config
from .compare import compare
from .licenses import terms_for
from .pipeline import PipelineError, run, run_from_cloud, run_text


def _common(p: argparse.ArgumentParser) -> None:
    p.add_argument("--config", required=True)
    p.add_argument("--backend", required=True)
    p.add_argument("--out", default="out")
    p.add_argument("--faces", type=int, help="decimate meshes to at most this many faces")
    p.add_argument("--commercial", action="store_true", help="you intend to use the result commercially")
    p.add_argument("--param", action="append", default=[], metavar="KEY=VALUE")


def _params(items: list[str]) -> dict:
    return dict(p.split("=", 1) for p in items if "=" in p)


def _report(res) -> int:
    print(json.dumps({"model": str(res.model), "record": str(res.record), "stats": res.stats}, indent=2))
    for w in res.warnings:
        print("LICENCE NOTE:", w, file=sys.stderr)
    return 0


def _execute(kind: str, source: str, backend, *, out, params, commercial, faces, cloud=False):
    if kind == "image":
        return run(source, backend, out, params=params, commercial_use=commercial, max_faces=faces,
                   want="cloud" if cloud else "mesh")
    if kind == "text":
        return run_text(source, backend, out, params=params, commercial_use=commercial, max_faces=faces,
                        want="cloud" if cloud else "mesh")
    return run_from_cloud(source, backend, out, params=params, commercial_use=commercial, max_faces=faces)


def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(prog="atelier3d", description="Image or text to 3D with a verifiable provenance record.")
    sub = ap.add_subparsers(dest="cmd", required=True)
    for name, help_ in (("image", "image -> model"), ("text", "text prompt -> model"), ("cloud", "point cloud -> model")):
        p = sub.add_parser(name, help=help_)
        p.add_argument("source")
        _common(p)
        if name != "cloud":
            p.add_argument("--cloud", action="store_true", help="stop at the point-cloud stage (.ply)")
    m = sub.add_parser("manifest", help="repeat a run described in a JSON file")
    m.add_argument("file")
    m.add_argument("--config", required=True)
    c = sub.add_parser("compare", help="compare two models")
    c.add_argument("a"); c.add_argument("b")
    v = sub.add_parser("verify", help="check a file against its provenance record")
    v.add_argument("model")
    b = sub.add_parser("backends", help="list configured backends and their licences")
    b.add_argument("--config", required=True)
    args = ap.parse_args(argv)

    if args.cmd == "verify":
        problems = provenance.verify(args.model)
        print("OK — file matches its provenance record" if not problems else "\n".join("PROBLEM: " + p for p in problems))
        return 0 if not problems else 1
    if args.cmd == "compare":
        try:
            print(json.dumps(compare(args.a, args.b), indent=2))
        except (OSError, ValueError) as exc:
            print(f"error: {exc}", file=sys.stderr)
            return 1
        return 0

    backends = load_config(args.config)
    if args.cmd == "backends":
        for name, be in backends.items():
            t = terms_for(be.license_id)
            print(f"{name:20} {t.name} (commercial: {t.commercial})")
        return 0

    if args.cmd == "manifest":
        spec = json.loads(Path(args.file).read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
        kind = next((k for k in ("image", "text", "cloud") if k in spec.get("input", {})), None)
        if kind is None or spec.get("backend") not in backends:
            print("error: manifest needs input.image|text|cloud and a configured backend", file=sys.stderr)
            return 2
        try:
            return _report(_execute(kind, spec["input"][kind], backends[spec["backend"]], out=spec.get("out", "out"),
                                    params=spec.get("params", {}), commercial=bool(spec.get("commercial")),
                                    faces=spec.get("faces"), cloud=bool(spec.get("stop_at_cloud"))))
        except PipelineError as exc:
            print(f"error: {exc}", file=sys.stderr)
            return 1

    if args.backend not in backends:
        print(f"unknown backend {args.backend!r}; configured: {', '.join(backends) or 'none'}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 2
    try:
        return _report(_execute(args.cmd, args.source, backends[args.backend], out=args.out, params=_params(args.param),
                                commercial=args.commercial, faces=args.faces, cloud=getattr(args, "cloud", False)))
    except PipelineError as exc:
        print(f"error: {exc}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 1


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())

"""The flows that matter: image, text or point cloud in — verified output plus provenance record out."""
from __future__ import annotations

import hashlib
import re
import shutil
import tempfile
import time
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Callable

from . import provenance
from .backends import Backend, BackendError
from .finish import decimate
from .glbcheck import GlbError, inspect_file as inspect_glb
from .licenses import terms_for, warnings as license_warnings
from .ply import PlyError, inspect_file as inspect_ply

ALLOWED_IMAGES = {".png", ".jpg", ".jpeg", ".webp"}
MAX_IMAGE_BYTES = 25 * 1024 * 1024
MAX_PROMPT_CHARS = 2000


class PipelineError(RuntimeError):
    pass


@dataclass
class Result:
    model: Path
    record: Path
    stats: dict
    warnings: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)


def _check_image(image: Path) -> None:
    if not image.is_file():
        raise PipelineError(f"image not found: {image}")
    if image.suffix.lower() not in ALLOWED_IMAGES:
        raise PipelineError(f"unsupported image type {image.suffix!r}; use one of {sorted(ALLOWED_IMAGES)}")
    if image.stat().st_size > MAX_IMAGE_BYTES:
        raise PipelineError("image is larger than 25 MB")


def _slug(text: str) -> str:
    return re.sub(r"[^a-z0-9]+", "-", text.lower()).strip("-")[:40] or "model"


def _execute(*, backend: Backend, source: Path, input_meta: dict, stem: str, out_dir: Path, params: dict,
             commercial_use: bool, max_faces: int | None, want: str, clock: Callable[[], float]) -> Result:
    """Shared engine. `want` is 'mesh' (a .glb) or 'cloud' (a .ply point cloud)."""
    out_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    started = clock()
    ext = ".glb" if want == "mesh" else ".ply"
    inspect = inspect_glb if want == "mesh" else inspect_ply
    bad = GlbError if want == "mesh" else PlyError

    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix="atelier3d-") as tmp:
        raw = Path(tmp) / ("raw" + ext)
        try:
            backend.generate(source, raw, params)
        except BackendError as exc:
            raise PipelineError(str(exc)) from exc
        if not raw.is_file() or raw.stat().st_size == 0:
            raise PipelineError(f"{backend.name} reported success but produced no file")
        try:
            inspect(raw)
        except bad as exc:
            raise PipelineError(f"{backend.name} produced an unusable {want}: {exc}") from exc

        steps: list[str] = []
        final_src = raw
        if max_faces and want == "mesh":
            slim = Path(tmp) / "slim.glb"
            steps.append(decimate(raw, slim, max_faces))
            final_src = slim

        stats = inspect(final_src).as_dict()
        model = out_dir / f"{stem}-{provenance.sha256_file(final_src)[:10]}{ext}"
        shutil.copyfile(final_src, model)

    terms = terms_for(backend.license_id)
    notes = license_warnings(backend.license_id, commercial_use)
    record = provenance.build(
        input_meta=input_meta, model=model, backend={"name": backend.name, "version": backend.version},
        params=params, license_id=terms.id, license_name=terms.name, commercial_use=commercial_use,
        warnings=notes, stats=stats, started=started, finished=clock(), finish_steps=steps)
    return Result(model, provenance.write(record, model), stats, notes)


def run(image: str | Path, backend: Backend, out_dir: str | Path, *, params: dict | None = None,
        commercial_use: bool = False, max_faces: int | None = None, want: str = "mesh",
        clock: Callable[[], float] = time.time) -> Result:
    """Image → mesh (or → point cloud with want='cloud')."""
    image = Path(image)
    _check_image(image)
    meta = {"kind": "image", "name": image.name, "sha256": provenance.sha256_file(image)}
    return _execute(backend=backend, source=image, input_meta=meta, stem=image.stem, out_dir=Path(out_dir),
                    params={**(params or {}), "mode": "image"}, commercial_use=commercial_use,
                    max_faces=max_faces, want=want, clock=clock)


def run_text(prompt: str, backend: Backend, out_dir: str | Path, *, params: dict | None = None,
             commercial_use: bool = False, max_faces: int | None = None, want: str = "mesh",
             clock: Callable[[], float] = time.time) -> Result:
    """Text prompt → mesh (or → point cloud). The prompt is hashed and stored in the record."""
    prompt = prompt.strip()
    if not prompt:
        raise PipelineError("prompt is empty")
    if len(prompt) > MAX_PROMPT_CHARS:
        raise PipelineError(f"prompt is longer than {MAX_PROMPT_CHARS} characters")
    meta = {"kind": "text", "sha256": hashlib.sha256(prompt.encode()).hexdigest(), "prompt": prompt}
    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix="atelier3d-prompt-") as tmp:
        src = Path(tmp) / "prompt.txt"
        src.write_text(prompt, encoding="utf-8")
        return _execute(backend=backend, source=src, input_meta=meta, stem=_slug(prompt), out_dir=Path(out_dir),
                        params={**(params or {}), "mode": "text", "prompt": prompt},
                        commercial_use=commercial_use, max_faces=max_faces, want=want, clock=clock)


def run_from_cloud(cloud: str | Path, backend: Backend, out_dir: str | Path, *, params: dict | None = None,
                   commercial_use: bool = False, max_faces: int | None = None,
                   clock: Callable[[], float] = time.time) -> Result:
    """Point cloud → mesh. The cloud's record digest is stored as the parent, so lineage is traceable."""
    cloud = Path(cloud)
    if not cloud.is_file():
        raise PipelineError(f"point cloud not found: {cloud}")
    try:
        inspect_ply(cloud)
    except PlyError as exc:
        raise PipelineError(f"point cloud is unusable: {exc}") from exc
    meta = {"kind": "pointcloud", "name": cloud.name, "sha256": provenance.sha256_file(cloud)}
    parent = provenance.sidecar_path(cloud)
    if parent.exists():
        meta["parent_record_digest"] = provenance.load_digest(parent)
    return _execute(backend=backend, source=cloud, input_meta=meta, stem=cloud.stem, out_dir=Path(out_dir),
                    params={**(params or {}), "mode": "cloud-to-mesh"}, commercial_use=commercial_use,
                    max_faces=max_faces, want="mesh", clock=clock)

def make_glb(triangles=2, meshes=1, truncate=0):
    doc = {"asset": {"version": "2.0"},
           "meshes": [{"primitives": [{"attributes": {"POSITION": 0}, "indices": 1}]} for _ in range(meshes)],
           "accessors": [{"count": triangles * 3}, {"count": triangles * 3}]}
    if meshes == 0:
        doc["meshes"] = []
    js = json.dumps(doc).encode()
    js += b" " * (-len(js) % 4)
    data = struct.pack("<III", 0x46546C67, 2, 12 + 8 + len(js)) + struct.pack("<II", len(js), 0x4E4F534A) + js
    return data[:-truncate] if truncate else data


class FakeBackend:
    name, license_id, version = "fake", "hunyuan-community", "1"

    def __init__(self, data=None):
        self.data = make_glb() if data is None else data

    def generate(self, image, out, params):
        out.write_bytes(self.data)

def test_ply_validation(tmp_path):
    from atelier3d.ply import PlyError, inspect_ply, write_ply
    good = tmp_path / "g.ply"
    write_ply(good, [(0, 0, 0), (2, 3, 4)])
    s = inspect_ply(good.read_bytes())
    assert s.points == 2 and s.bounds_max == (2.0, 3.0, 4.0) and not s.has_color
    same = tmp_path / "s.ply"
    write_ply(same, [(1, 1, 1), (1, 1, 1)])
    for data in (b"junk", same.read_bytes(), good.read_bytes()[:-4]):
        with pytest.raises(PlyError):
            inspect_ply(data)
    ascii_ply = b"ply\nformat ascii 1.0\nelement vertex 2\nproperty float x\nproperty float y\nproperty float z\nend_header\n0 0 0\n1 2 3\n"
    assert inspect_ply(ascii_ply).points == 2
    nan = b"ply\nformat ascii 1.0\nelement vertex 2\nproperty float x\nproperty float y\nproperty float z\nend_header\n0 0 0\nnan 1 1\n"
    with pytest.raises(PlyError, match="NaN"):
